transcript:
Meeting Header
Date/Time: 2026-05-03 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Tom Barrett (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (OrionCloud PM), Sara Malik (OrionCloud Eng), Alex Rivera (OrionCloud SA), Nadia Ortiz (OrionCloud Product)

Summary: Quick technical sync to map out what OrionCloud needs to list Redwood-powered joint solution in their marketplace and to align on a reference architecture repo and pilot. Covering SSO, billing, images, terraform modules, private deployment options, and co-marketing assets.

[00:00] Tom Barrett: hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Tom from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer
[00:10] Priya Nair: hey hi, quick note: we'll mostly be looking at the integration points for the marketplace listing and the reference arch, and then map out next steps
[00:18] Liam Chen: thanks Tom right, we wanna make sure the listing is straightforward and that the reference arch covers our VPC patterns, like how customers can deploy redwood privately inside OrionCloud's managed vpc offering
[00:29] Sara Malik: yeah also network egress costs are a big thing for us, and we want to call out supported instance types, gpu counts, and quantified latency expectations in the reference doc
[00:38] Alex Rivera: can you also define the entitlements model? like how will billing/seat or token-based metering appear inside OrionCloud marketplace?
[00:46] Tom Barrett: good q; there are two options: Redwood-hosted billing where we invoice and OrionCloud receives referral fees, or marketplace entitlements where you bill end customers and we integrate usage reporting. Both are possible, depends on OrionCloud's marketplace capabilities
[00:59] Priya Nair: technical constraints to think about: SSO/SAML for admin portal, KMS integration for key management if customer wants private deployment, and a reference terraform module so customers can bootstrap a private deployment with minimal manual steps
[01:15] Nadia Ortiz: for marketing we need a clean solution brief and a screenshot of the console flow; also what kind of support level can we promise in the listing?
[01:23] Tom Barrett: we can template support SLAs in the listing - standard, premium - and we can include contact/CSM info in the back of the listing
[01:31] Liam Chen: on the reference arch, from Orion side we have managed VPC offering where we want to provide a marketplace tile that can create a private deployment into the customer's project. important: network isolation, use of our KMS, and maybe a sidecar pattern for audit logs
[01:46] Priya Nair: ok so two reference-arch flavors: 1) Redwood-hosted marketplace offering (fast onboarding, Redwood runtime in our infra) and 2) Private deployment via OrionCloud managed VPC (customer-owned infra). we'll capture both in docs and terraform examples
[01:59] Sara Malik: slight typo in our internal notes, we call it "Redwoood Dedicated" sometimes, ignore that, lol, transcripts will have that too
[02:05] Alex Rivera: real quick, what's your recommended way to handle KV cache and model variants for multi-tenant deployments so we don't blow memory?
[02:12] Priya Nair: good question - recommend per-tenant prefixing of KV caches, plus an eviction policy; we also suggest model-variant routing rules in the smart routing layer: e.g., route to quantized variants for low-cost tiers, full-fp models for premium customers
[02:28] Liam Chen: about certs and KMS, if our customers insist on using their own HSM, is that supported?
[02:34] Priya Nair: yes, for private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations, but it adds a provisioning step. need to document key rotation and audit log flow too
[02:43] Tom Barrett: also note SOC 2 and audit logs are baked into the platform; we can share the security pack but you'll need to confirm which artifacts Orion wants to display in the marketplace listing
[02:55] Nadia Ortiz: can you send that security pack? security folks will need to review for marketplace compliance
[03:00] Tom Barrett: yep I'll drop the security/ SOC2 and compliance documents in the shared drive after this call
[03:07] Alex Rivera: on the marketplace tile, what artifacts do you need for the image and startup script? we use a provider model where the tile can create infra and bootstrap the service
[03:15] Priya Nair: we'd want a small bootstrap script, container images (or AMI), and terraform module. we can provide a slim container that contacts Redwood control plane to register instances, with optional flags for VPC endpoints and custom KMS
[03:29] Sara Malik: for the private deployments, our networking team requires ip whitelisting, peering, or a transit gateway pattern; which network topologies does Redwood support?
[03:38] Priya Nair: we support peering, transit gateway, and VPC endpoints. we'll add diagrams for each pattern in the reference arch: peering for small customers, transit for large enterprises, and endpoint+NAT for restricted setups
[03:52] Liam Chen: timeline expectations - how long from tile approval to listing?
[03:56] Tom Barrett: typical is 2-4 weeks if both teams provide assets quickly; the long pole is security review and any legal billing integration. marketplace listing approvals vary by operator though
[04:08] Alex Rivera: also need health-checking hooks and traces; can we ship a small tracing agent or configure Jaeger/OTEL exporters?
[04:15] Priya Nair: yes we expose tracing hooks and can push OTEL exporters; Redwood Console supports per-route tracing and token-level cost breakdowns - we'll show examples in the reference arch doc
[04:29] Nadia Ortiz: do you have a sample listing we can mirror visually?
[04:33] Tom Barrett: yes I'll share a sample screenshot and the listing markdown template
[04:37] Sara Malik: on the benchmarks: we want to run a short PoC end-to-end - can your team define a standard benchmark harness we can run in OrionCloud?
[04:46] Priya Nair: we have a lightweight harness that runs synthetic throughput/latency tests and token-cost reports; we'll provide the harness and a script to run it against hosted endpoints and private deployment
[04:58] Liam Chen: are there licensing constraints if we list on OrionCloud marketplace? like co-marketing exclusivity or revenue share minimums?
[05:05] Tom Barrett: legal will handle the revenue share; from a tech perspective there's no exclusivity requirement, but if you want any co-marketing commitments we can document them in an MOU
[05:14] Alex Rivera: one more ops question: what metrics are surfaced to a tenant admin? CPU/GPU usage, token consumption, model versions in use?
[05:22] Priya Nair: yes, Console exposes token burn by route, per-instance GPU usage, per-model latency percentiles, and KV cache hit rates. we'll include dashboard screenshots and an API example for pulling those metrics into OrionCloud's billing/usage system
[05:38] Sara Malik: small nit: spelling of "KV cache" sometimes comes out as "K V cash" in transcripts, just FYI when you look at the notes
[05:45] Tom Barrett: ha noted. ok let's talk pilot success criteria - Liam?
[05:49] Liam Chen: for us pilot success is: automated tile deploys a private Redwood runtime into a customer VPC, <200ms p95 for our typical 4k token prompts, and stability for 48 hours under a 50rps synthetic load. plus the listing metadata and support docs live in the marketplace
[06:06] Priya Nair: that's reasonable. we'll help run the benchmarks and instrument the app. also propose a canary rollout plan in the ref-arch for safe upgrades
[06:18] Alex Rivera: ok timeline: if we get the terraform and archetecture docs by 2026-05-14 we can aim for pilot kickoff 2026-05-25
[06:27] Tom Barrett: sounds good. I'll send over the marketplace checklist and security pack now. Priya will start the terraform repo and we'll sync next week for a demo build session
[06:36] Nadia Ortiz: thanks all, great session
[06:39] Tom Barrett: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the action items

Notes on transcript quality: Auto-transcription had a few mishears on product names and acronyms (Redwoood, K V cash). Speaker boundaries are mostly correct but a couple of quick crosstalk bits are merged.

References/shared artifacts mentioned:
- Redwood marketplace listing template (link to shared drive)
- Redwood security pack / SOC2 summary (link)
- Reference-arch terraform repo (to be created)
- Benchmark harness and scripts (link)

End of transcript.
